fieldNotes.facility: GM Wentzville Assembly, 1500 E Route A, Wentzville MO. Geocode point (38.8181,-90.8211) lands on the main contiguous assembly + stamping building - identity unambiguous. 3.7M sq ft under roof on ~440-569 acres; builds Chevrolet Colorado / GMC Canyon midsize pickups and Chevrolet Express / GMC Savana full-size vans. Opened 1983.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Site is fully fenced/walled: Street View on the west perimeter road shows continuous chain-link fence; the SW public approach shows a long white screening wall with a manicured gated entry drive. Main plant entrance road meets Route A at a signalized intersection (pano mIjMjF5N2Oi8ADmhAOvjqA); the manned guard gate sits inboard on plant property beyond public Street View reach. Controlled truck entrance confirmed by perimeter security + auto-plant standard.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Not directly visible in Street View (guard post is inside the fence line, off public roads), but a secured OEM assembly plant of this scale with full perimeter fencing/walls and a single controlled material-receiving entrance is universally manned-gate. Called true at high confidence per facility type and security evidence; the booth structure itself was not individually resolved.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False - manned guard gate assumed, not a kiosk-only remote check-in.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: Trucks enter/exit through the same controlled material-gate group near the NW building face off the Route A access road.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Wide paved aprons inside the fence in front of the NW dock face provide internal queue/holding room.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long internal approach from the Route A intersection to the receiving docks easily holds 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: The Route A access road and internal aprons are very wide with unused paved width - room to add a bypass/express lane.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 50+ band. Integrated 3.7M sq ft plant with material-receiving docks tucked under canopies and recessed faces on multiple building faces plus a detached east warehouse/body building; individual doors are obscured by roof canopies from overhead so the count (estimated ~70) is approximate - flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 25-50 band estimate. Trailer drop/parking along the NW material yard separate from the vast finished-vehicle marshalling lots (those hold cars, not trailers). Count is an overhead estimate - flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer staging along the NW dock yard, distinct from the finished-vehicle storage lots that dominate the north and northeast.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Inbound parts/material receiving (truck + rail material docks on the W/NW/E faces) is physically separate from outbound finished-vehicle shipping (rail autorack loading at the SW rail yard and vehicle haulaway from the marshalling lots).
fieldNotes.railServed: Major multi-track rail classification yard immediately SW of the plant with autorack rail cars staged; rail spurs run into the property along the south. Definitive rail service.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Integrated campus: main assembly building, contiguous stamping facility, a large detached building on the east face, and a north sequencing/supplier building - multiple large structures on one property.
fieldNotes.multiStep: Controlled perimeter gate plus internal yard checkpoints typical of a secured OEM plant; layered access. Medium-confidence inference.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale clearly resolved in the imagery; left false and flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Wentzville is an outer-edge exurb ~40 mi west of St. Louis off I-70; the plant is bordered by farmland, woods, and a rail corridor. Per rubric, choose Rural over small-town industrial.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Wide divided access road suggests ~2 inbound lanes at the gate; overhead estimate, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: 470 acres computed from the traced perimeter ring, consistent with the cited ~440-569 acre site.

citations.claim: GM Wentzville Assembly currently builds the Chevrolet Colorado and GMC Canyon; GM-operated plant
Wentzville was NOT on GM's 2009 bankruptcy plant-closure list; retained by New GM

verification.rationale: GM-owned, self-operated assembly plant actively building Colorado/Canyon in 2025; explicitly retained through the 2009 bankruptcy (not divested to MLC/RACER).
